posts.title: Prepare time reports and invoices for review
posts.promise: Extract key fields from sample records and leave every figure for a person to check.
posts.whatItIs: A fresh paid administrator vacancy names handling time reports and invoicing. A small student experiment could read fictional time reports and invoices, place selected fields in a spreadsheet, and flag missing or inconsistent entries. That AI workflow is a proposed design, not a tool demonstrated by the notice.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a professional-services office with recurring time-report and invoice preparation may pay for setup or use. The vacancy establishes paid human work, not demand for an AI service or actual buyer willingness.
loop: Use fictional time reports and invoices as inputs.
Extract proposed fields such as dates, hours, invoice total and reference.
Check required fields and flag blanks or mismatched totals.
Place extracted values and source filenames in a review sheet.
A person verifies every value and decides whether to enter it into real records.
posts.evidence: The official paid-work notice says the administrator should be comfortable handling time reports and invoicing. It does not describe the documents, task frequency, software, or any AI product.
posts.uncertainty: The prototype should use fictional test records only. Field choices, spreadsheet output and checks are design choices; extraction can misread figures, and a human must confirm records before billing or payment.
first24Hours: Create three fictional time-report and invoice pairs with varied dates and totals.
Build a spreadsheet with proposed fields and a missing-value flag.
Try manual extraction and a simple AI-assisted pass, then compare every field against the fictional originals.
